frequency_question: How often have multi-step regulatory capital rulemakings (specifically those involving complex public comment and inter-agency coordination) been initiated and fully executed from proposal to final effective rule within a tight calendar horizon of approximately three to six months?
membership_rule: Includes any Federal Reserve Board rulemakings under Regulation Q or related capital frameworks that proceeded from a formal notice of proposed rulemaking (NPR) to a final rule. Excludes routine technical corrections or emergency interim final rules that bypass standard comment windows.

cases.name: Holistic Capital Review (Basel III Endgame) Proposal Stage

coverage_note: 5 major capital rulemaking cycles examined; 1 completed within a compressed timeline under 6 months.
known_gaps: Excludes minor amendments that do not require full public notice-and-comment periods.
skeleton: Regulatory rulemakings of this structural complexity requiring public notice, quantitative impact studies, and board votes.
multiplier: 5 historical major rule iterations / 1 successful rapid-completion instance within a sub-six-month window
validity_reason: Administrative Procedure Act statutory notice-and-comment requirements remain legally fixed and invariant over this timeframe.
